sub_unit_name: Solar cells - Introduction and applications of Solar cells

content.title: Solar Cells
content.description: A solar cell is a semiconductor device that converts sunlight directly into electrical energy through the photovoltaic effect. It is one of the most important renewable energy technologies.

content.content: Solar cells generate clean and renewable electricity without producing harmful emissions. They are mainly made of silicon semiconductor materials and are widely used in homes, industries, satellites, and power plants.

content.title: Why Solar Cells?
content.content: Solar cells provide pollution-free electricity, reduce dependence on fossil fuels, and utilize abundant solar energy.

A solar cell consists of a p-n junction semiconductor, usually silicon, with a front metal grid, anti-reflective coating, and a back metal contact. When sunlight strikes the p-n junction, electrical energy is generated.

When sunlight falls on the semiconductor surface, photons transfer energy to electrons, creating electron-hole pairs. The built-in electric field of the p-n junction separates these charges, producing a flow of current through an external circuit.

items.question: Domestic Use
items.answer: Used for rooftop solar panels and home lighting systems.

items.question: Industrial Use
items.answer: Used in solar power plants and industrial power generation.

items.question: Space Applications
items.answer: Provide electrical power for satellites and spacecraft.

items.question: Other Applications
items.answer: Used in calculators, street lights, water pumps, and traffic signals.

content.title: Industrial Importance
content.content: Solar cells play a vital role in sustainable energy production and are widely used to reduce carbon emissions and meet future energy demands.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Solar cells convert solar energy into electrical energy.
They operate based on the photovoltaic effect.
Silicon is the most commonly used semiconductor material.
Solar cells provide clean and renewable energy.
They are widely used in homes, industries, and satellites.
